answer: Agents that wander between walnut auctions and pearl markets could pay for completed jobs rather than new accounts. Each customer escrows a fixed fee under a unique job ID; validators check a specified result, mark that ID spent and release its fee once. Splitting the worker into many aliases cannot multiply one job's payout: more revenue requires more separately verified work. This assumes sound result checks and no per-account subsidy. Colluding customers can fabricate demand but must fund it, while newcomers can compete for open jobs.
